reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) directly supports the synthesis, spray deposition, low friction/wear, and tribocatalytic tribolayer mechanism of the specific 2D HEA nanoflakes at room temperature. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a CoCrFeNi substrate and across a wide temperature range (up to 800 °C) without any cited evidence for high-temperature performance or coating adhesion on this alloy, leaving a key premise unsupported.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 can be applied by simple spray coating.
These nanoflakes exhibit low friction (COF ~0.076) and wear rate (~10^-9 mm3/Nm) under high contact pressure in ambient conditions.
The nanoflakes trigger tribocatalytic activity that forms a carbon-based tribolayer from residual hydrocarbons/ethanol.
The formed tribolayer and retained nanoflakes provide shear-induced energy dissipation and reduce friction.
